p2_verdicts.title: main layer glue zero coverage
p2_verdicts.evidence: TestMainGlue (tests/test_a1_phase4.py:384-515) has 7 cases mapping 1:1 onto the glue functions and they assert real state, not just execution: test_ensure_skips_unknown_and_negative_ids (tests:398-406) asserts store.all_keys()=={} AND proto.hsm.terminal_ids()==[] after _ensure_device_key(99)/(-5) (guards main.py:410-412); test_ensure_mints_only_for_enrolled_terminal (tests:408-423) asserts hsm.has_key(1), persisted keys=={1} after DeviceKeyStore(path).load(), and idempotence (second call still 1 key); test_cmd_setkey_flow (tests:425-440) asserts the golden R2 through the HSM (hsm.respond(W3_FIRST_C2,terminal_id=1)==W3_FIRST_R2 proves the key reached the HSM) plus disk state {1:W3_KEY}, and its 5 bad-input tuples (tests:435) hit all 4 error branches of cmd_setkey (usage main.py:566-568, fromhex ValueError :572-574, length :575-578, tid<0 :579-581) with a store-unchanged assertion afterwards; test_cmd_c2reset_flow (tests:442-457) asserts protocol window [], persisted window [], AND the behaviour that W3_FIRST_C2 is re-accepted as MSG_CHALLENGE; test_flush_persists_and_swallows_oserror (tests:459-478) asserts persisted [W3_FIRST_C2] then that a monkeypatched OSError is swallowed with 'persistence failed' printed (main.py:437-438); test_repl_survives_store_oserror (tests:480-494) asserts rc==0 + '[ERROR]' via repl's OSError handler (main.py:688-692); test_repl_smoke_setkey_auth_quit_golden_r2 (tests:496-515) drives the setkey->auth->quit REPL sequence and asserts rc==0, 'PASS' and golden R2 '7b45b0545e59aa94' in output (flip_prob=0 at tests:509).

p2_verdicts.title: late-C2 override branches untested (on_response/on_extra_response + _finish_pass None fallback)
p2_verdicts.evidence: TestLateC2 (tests:267-335) covers _update_session_c2 (protocol.py:586-609) branch by branch on the on_response path: (1) late binding accepted -> test_late_binding_sets_r2 (tests:284-293, start_auth without c2 then on_response(c2=W3_FIRST_C2) -> PASS with R2==W3_FIRST_R2); (2) late binding refused as replay -> test_late_binding_rejected_as_replay (tests:295-302, pre-seeded history then same C2 -> ProtocolError, pinning protocol.py:600-604); (3) mid-session conflict -> test_c2_conflict_mid_session first half (tests:310-312, c2^0xFF -> ProtocolError, protocol.py:606-609); (4) harmless restatement -> same test second half (tests:313-315, restate original c2 -> PASS, R2==Speck(K,c2)); (5) None fallback -> test_no_c2_fallback_r2_is_speck_of_zero_block (tests:317-325, exact assertion R2==Speck6496(W3_KEY).encrypt(bytes(8)) pinning protocol.py:619); (6) HSM failure branch of _finish_pass -> test_hsm_failure_answers_result_error_frame (tests:327-335, SpeckHSM() without keys -> (MSG_RESULT, result=2, hd=0xFF), protocol.py:620-628). Mutation control MUT-C (in-memory removal of the _remember_c2 gate in _update_session_c2) turns the suite RED at test_late_binding_rejected_as_replay, proving the protection is real, not incidental.
p2_verdicts.residual: The second call site named by the original finding -- on_extra_response, protocol.py:512 -- remains completely untested, together with the whole gray-zone path; recorded as new finding N1 below rather than STILL_BROKEN because the shared _update_session_c2 logic itself is now pinned by 5 tests on the primary path and the original safety concern (C2 deciding R2) has substantive coverage.

p2_verdicts.title: restart replay-window E2E missing
p2_verdicts.evidence: TestRestartReplayE2E.test_replayed_c2_refused_after_restart (tests:341-381) walks the real persistence round-trip: run #1 wires store1->SpeckHSM(keys=store1.all_keys())->HFIDAProtocol exactly like main() (main.py:741-749), mints the key via _ensure_device_key, obtains c2 from transport.counter_challenge(1) (the terminal counter), passes on_access_request -> MSG_CHALLENGE, then persists via _flush_c2_state(proto1, store1) (main.py:423-438). The 'restart' half builds FRESH objects only: store2 = DeviceKeyStore(keys_path).load() (reloaded from disk, tests:366), hsm2 = SpeckHSM(keys=store2.all_keys()) with has_key(1) asserted (tests:367-368), brand-new templates2/pools2/proto2, and rehydrates history with the same loop shape as main.py:750-751 (tests:372-373). proto1/proto2 share no state, so the asserted RESULT_REPLAY on the replayed C2 (tests:375-377) can only come from the disk-rehydrated window; the fresh-C2-accepted assertion (tests:379-381) rules out a degenerate reject-everything protocol. This is NOT a same-object replay.
p2_verdicts.residual: main() itself (argparse, serial branch, nested finally, main.py:734-773) has no direct test -- the test mirrors its wiring, as FIXLIST honestly states. Mirror-wiring is an acceptable compromise; direct main() coverage listed as observation N4.

flake_quantification.detail: Every verdict-carrying path now pins flip_prob=0.0 (tests:247, 259, 289, 300, 309, 321, 332 pass it explicitly; tests:509 sets terminal.flip_prob=0.0). At prob=0 SimulatedTerminal.respond never enters the flip loop (main.py:129 'if prob > 0.0'), so _rng is never consulted; hd is deterministically 0 <= TAU_PASS*n and decide_scaled returns PASS (threshold.py:87, TAU_PASS=6). Remaining randomness is value-only, not branch/verdict randomness: terminal secret token_bytes(32) (main.py:113) changes seed material but templates enrol from the same secret's ideal_response so hd stays 0; DeviceKeyStore.key_for mints random keys but assertions are same-source comparisons (key2==key across reload). Quantification of the ORIGINAL exposure (for the record): at p=0.02 the 4x64-bit aggregate HD is ~Poisson(5.12); P(sum >= 25, the gray-zone onset) is ~1e-9 per round -- mechanically real, practically unobservable; P3 was the right severity and the de-randomisation kills it entirely.
flake_quantification.leftovers: LoopbackTransport._rng (main.py:154) is a dead attribute never used by any method (observation, no flake impact); SerialTransport.counter_challenge=secrets.token_bytes(8) (main.py:205) is untouched by tests and already in the deferred list (W3 receive loop).

loopback_counter_consistency.detail: LoopbackTransport.counter_challenge (main.py:163-165) delegates directly to self.terminal(tid).counter_challenge() -- one shared counter, no independent state. SimulatedTerminal.C2_INIT=bytes(0xA0+j) (main.py:109) matches terminal_fsm.v:150 (c2_counter[j] = 8'hA0 + j[7:0]); the pre-increment-then-emit order (main.py:145-146) matches terminal_fsm.v:402-403 (counter and tx_buf[8+k] both take c2_counter[k]+1, so first auth emits a1..a8); bytewise no-carry wrap matches the per-byte RTL increment. Pinned by tests: TestSimulatedTerminalC2 asserts the exact first three values AND the exact 0x5F wraparound 00..07 / 01..08 (tests:522-534, P3#8 fix in place); TestEndToEnd:243 asserts transport.counter_challenge(1) == W3_FIRST_C2, i.e. the transport path itself yields the golden first C2.

new_findings.description: The gray-zone re-test path on_extra_response (protocol.py:490-517) has ZERO test coverage across the entire suite -- including the second call site of _update_session_c2 (protocol.py:512) that the P2-T2 fix introduced. No test reaches session state GRAY, so MSG_EXTRA_CHALLENGE framing, the 7-response aggregate scaled threshold (design P1-6), gray-path pool consumption, _finish_reject and the C2 late-bind/conflict/restatement semantics on this path are all unprotected. Mutation-proven: an in-memory mutant deleting the _update_session_c2 call from on_extra_response passes all 33 tests (MUT-A), whereas the identical regression on on_response is caught (MUT-C). All flip_prob=0 tests deterministically land at hd_sum=0, so GRAY is never even reachable with the current fixtures; reaching it needs a crafted impostor/partial-flip responder.

cmd_enroll (main.py:475-509) -- including the P3#3 fix's enrollment-then-mint ordering (main.py:507-509) -- is never invoked by any test; fixtures call templates.enroll()/pools.reserve() directly. Mutation-proven unprotected: swallowing cmd_enroll's trailing _ensure_device_key leaves all 33 tests green (MUT-B), i.e. a regression that re-orders or drops the mint would ship silently. The _ensure gate itself IS protected (test_ensure_skips_unknown_and_negative_ids), only the cmd_enroll wiring is not. Behaviour smoke (MUT-D) confirms the current path works (enroll 1 10 -> [ENROLL], has_key(1) True).

The REPL 'spoof' command path has zero coverage: repl dispatch (main.py:671-672) -> cmd_auth(impostor=True) -> LoopbackTransport.respond impostor branch (main.py:177-179, fresh SimulatedTerminal(-1-tid)). This is the W5 mutual-exclusion demo path. Behaviour smoke (MUT-D) shows 'spoof 1' correctly ends in REJECT after a successful 'enroll'+'auth', so it is a pure coverage gap.
